title: The Row Stood Where It Stood

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Three askings do not make a witness. The weather answers the first, the price of barley the second; the third goes up the terrace while the row stands where it stood. A witness stands somewhere and can be asked, and nobody stood.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Clay Yard, told in the last tend of Grain

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and thirty-four to two hundred and thirty-six days, six months and fifty-four days to six months and fifty-six days, carried everywhere and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing --- the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing; the ownerless question opened as a surgeon opens a wound and found to have no witness at the bottom; a colour parted from a hearing and a shape parted from a seventh; the read figure held apart from the paid figure; the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost --- without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no hearing beyond six, no seventh of the full note, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no fifth telling of the burned slate, no third telling of the counting room shut in the war, no fourth shaping of the pot saying, no fifth witness to the question, no eighth green or eighth shape, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no opening of the widow's mark, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read, no figure given for the dressed grain or the hand that did not come back, no name spoken over the green or the shape, no sale or betrayal paid and no ending

scenes.title: The Fifty-Fourth Day
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap: Day 234, Grain 25, Fifthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf and the Clay Yard. No recap: the hand lay down against the fold after the forty-second answer and that two-rhythm coordination is set down like a tool, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. Count exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody at 233 going into **234**, six months and fifty-four days, told by nobody (T071/T072); first smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Three counts in three places --- the carried fire's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should be under the floor (payer unnamed two hundred and thirty-four days, T088), the river's note of water over water through the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot --- none rising into another, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). One leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. The file is turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers, three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings on their own places, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Grain's second arithmetic and the true subtraction in Berr's locked box answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, Seed 16 unspent, loan uncalled, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape, and the Grain 21 question on its seventh place with **two** askings and no witness standing (T101 held). The dressed grain lies covered and unfigured near the hearth, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm's weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate (T077). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, gives every instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket, says *the house* and *The house will keep it*, moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in **fifty-four** days, because a morning, a shelf and a basket are not openings (T058/T079/T100). A cost-question at the threshold goes to the pot and the weather, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). The hand is asked the first way of the chapter: up an inch toward the river's note and down at once under conditions that have sometimes answered --- **forty-third answer**, filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule. Grain 30 (Day 239), the third and last Account-day, stands five mornings ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it; the third asking is held for Scene 4.

scenes.title: Six Counted at the Sill
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 234, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot, into the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: salt-stiff coat with the crease at the left shoulder, hollow seat with its twenty-year lean and hollow, the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw unswept, a proverb gone years ago to a pot with no crack, the tile debt circling without a name, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-four days; no collector came up or went down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed and tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, setting the small knife at the very edge of its sill: six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check, the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it. The ear-sentence comes to his teeth and goes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name --- a remembered stopping and not a new one --- nine stoppings stand with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent, the loan stays uncalled and no collector came on Grain 25; chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, pale clip-ring at the left wrist, warm stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot in the Debt Loft, which reaches him as a sound with a direction and nothing more (T036/T076/T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray; three or more men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name and he does not say the room is cold. He speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), tells a pot *You'll do*, knows the full note it will give three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them; the burned-slate word stands at four and the two tellings of the counting room shut in the war stand at two, with a hand between them and the three sayings; he grows quieter and the household straightens around the quiet without an order, his quiet going before him into the shed the way a cold air goes before a door; *he's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise of the foundling's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). When Sella's voice goes low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence, takes the cold out of the fingertip and gives nothing back, holds until the sentence reaches the pot, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing --- a remembered repetition and not a change made again, joined to no kiln (T062). At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the clean dark line, the finer grey, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098 advanced, not paid). Small hours: no breathing number anywhere in the house, the two rooms do not touch, and the hand is asked the second way --- held to the small intake only and down before the letting-go --- **forty-fourth answer**, filed on the sixth place, not a power. Grain 30 holds five mornings off and the third asking is held for Scene 4.

scenes.title: The Cover Goes Back
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 235, Grain 26, Sixthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf and the Clay Yard. New day, new date, no recap: **235** exact, six months and fifty-five days, nobody told (T071/T072); fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty-five days (T088); first smell hot clay under tallow, first sound the kiln in fours with a gap, no bell, no market and no Cross. The dressed grain is turned under its wool for damp, looked at, spread thin to finish and gathered back by the handful, the fold set flat; it changes state and gains no figure, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm's weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate, and laid across none of the absences (T077). A neighbour at the threshold asks what the storing will take now the grain is under wool and Sella sends the question to the pot and the weather; a man come down the clay road brings a number up out of a fist toward the yard well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere --- nothing priced, refused or entered; the figure read over the covered basket on Grain's second Account-day is still not the figure paid, and the true subtraction stays locked in Berr's box answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 (T015/T041/T047 held). A wrong wind comes up off High Kiln: the sweet edge of lead glaze rides over the boards, touches the fold and goes out on the wind that brought it, a direction arrived nowhere and not a second edge paid, the seventh green still a colour and the seventh shape still a shape with no eighth of either, no second look joined, no name spoken over either, no loaf, slate or sale, neither woman nor child called Fenna nor Ulda in the narration and no romance paid (T064, T050/T051 and T033/T034 held); one of the three shapings of the pot saying --- a pot gone quiet on every row come the thaw --- is let to stand again as a saying, not a fourth likeness made a cause, with no lesson, no name for what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 and no pot lost (T061/T082). Sella moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in **fifty-five** days, because a morning, a shelf and a yard are not openings (T058/T079/T100). The hand is asked the third way: up an inch toward the river's low note, kept a moment, then down before the counted breath in the room that does not touch his has finished --- **forty-fifth answer**, filed on the sixth place with no payer named. The question's third asking is held for the afternoon of this day and not brought into the morning.

scenes.title: The Third Asking
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 235, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the boards fronting the shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. THE CHAPTER'S ONE MOVEMENT, advanced and not paid --- **T101 gains a third asking**: a voice with no owner, no room, no hand at the kiln and no cause comes over the boards again, low into the boards and not into the basket, asking which row the pot went quiet on. The weather answers first and the price of barley answers after it, and the voice goes off up the terrace while the row stands where it stood --- a direction arrived nowhere, with nobody leaning in to take the answer down. The boy takes it apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound --- what it asks, where it stands, what it would want before any man could answer it, and who would have to stand under the answer to pay --- and finds no witness at the bottom, setting the third telling on the seventh place beside the first two with a finger between each pair, and a finger between them and the three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling, the two shut-room tellings, the six hearings of the full note and the count. Three askings are not one witness; a witness stands somewhere and can be asked, and none does and none could. It is NOT a fourth shaping of the pot saying, NOT a hearing, NOT a seventh of the full note, NOT a fifth telling of the slate, NOT a cause, NOT a name and NOT a fifth witness --- a seed for the far-off day a witness stands somewhere and can be asked (T101 advanced, unpaid). Three sayings stay three, the burned-slate word stays at four and the shut-room tellings stay two (T061/T082, T035/T031/T065/T095). The afternoon thins; heat settles under the low angle into the fold where one stiff brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting; Garl stays kept in objects and his tile debt uncalled, with no collector in the road (T009/T013/T092). Sella tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the mark untouched --- no opening in fifty-five days (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn says *Six counted. The next I don't count*, stops the ear-sentence short of the calling word as a remembered stopping, holds nine with no tenth, keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076). At the wheel-shed Jorra's quiet goes before him and his bent finger goes into the damper ahead of the unfinished sentence, holds, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing as a remembered repetition (T062). Small hours: no breathing number anywhere, the two rooms do not touch; the hand is asked the fourth way --- kept to the river's own low interval with no count in the house to borrow, and down on the next low note --- **forty-sixth answer**, filed on the sixth place, not a power. Grain 30 holds four mornings off.

scenes.title: Fifty-Six Days Without an Opening
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 236, Grain 27, Seventhday, small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf and the Clay Yard. New day, new date, no recap: **236** exact, six months and fifty-six days, nobody told (T071/T072); fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty-six days (T088); first smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln in fours with its gap, no bell, no market, no Cross. Ordinary tending goes on: the dressed grain under wool is looked at for damp and gathered back under the fold, changed and unfigured, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm's weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and given no figure (T077). A cost-question at the door and another at the well go to the pot and the weather and away level; a fist's number come down the clay road goes back into its sleeve, arriving nowhere, and the neighbour at the loaf shelf who wants to know what the storing will take is sent to ask the pot, so nothing is priced, refused or entered (T077). A wrong wind off High Kiln brings the sweet edge of glaze over the boards, touches the fold and goes out on the wind that brought it --- a direction, not a second edge paid; the seventh green is a colour and the seventh shape a shape, gathered at Grain's first market and carried unjoined through the working mornings since, with no eighth of either, no second look joined, no name spoken over either, no loaf, slate or sale, no promotion into a hearing, a cause or a romance (T064, T050/T051 and T033/T034 held). Sella moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and leaves the widow's mark where it hangs --- no opening in **fifty-six** days, because a morning, a shelf, a yard and a basket are not openings (T058/T079/T100). The yard goes around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place; seven things standing in a row are still seven and not an account until somebody finds a payer to stand under them, and none does (T009/T013/T092, T098 advanced, not paid, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause). The hand is asked the fifth way: up an inch under conditions that had once answered and down at once, a miss entered and filed on the sixth place with no payer named --- **forty-seventh answer**, not a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule. The question stands over the boards with three askings and nobody to own it; Grain 30 (Day 239) stands three mornings ahead and is not brought early.

scenes.title: The Count Goes Forward
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 236, Grain 27, Seventhday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot, into the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: salt-stiff coat, hollow seat with its twenty-year lean, unswept clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw, proverb gone to a pot with no crack, tile debt circling without a name, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-six days; no collector came up or went down the clay road on Grain 25, 26 or 27 (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives the fire its instruction before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it* where another woman would say *I*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in fifty-six days (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, sets the knife at the very edge with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered stopping with no figure and no name, holds nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, his stroke over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch and over the collector's road without the half-check or a turn, the warm stone lying cold and unreconciled in its loft pot (T036/T076/T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust under the bent finger, dusty and clean forearms on one tray, gives the house no name for the men who went low before first grey, speaks to the wheel and tells a pot *You'll do*, withholds the note known three turns ahead, keeps the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, keeps *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise ungiven, and does not look toward the bed or the basket (T035/T031/T062/T061/T082). At the going of the light she carries him home at the half-pace and sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold right, thread frozen; goes to her own bed before the small hours and leaves the coals to keep themselves. In the small hours no breathing number sounds anywhere, the two rooms do not touch, and fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T061/T082). He turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers, the three sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings on their own places, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape fourth, the carried man's pale line fifth and the held inch sixth, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape, the dressed grain covered and unfigured, the returning-line place gone around with no number, and the Grain 21 question on its seventh place with **three** askings and nobody to own it (T101 advanced, unpaid). He puts the question to his hand the sixth way of the chapter: the hand goes up an inch toward the low note through the finger's-width door and stays; he takes it through the small intake, the hold and the letting-go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, keeps it through the little silence after her count has ended and brings it down on the river's next low note --- two rhythms held one against the other across a wall that does not touch, remembered, not a change made again, NOT a longer reach, miss entered, hearing, seventh, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named and not spent or explained: **forty-eighth answer**, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. Two hundred and thirty-six stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and fifty-six days told by nobody; the fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty-six days; the widow's mark untouched with no opening in fifty-six days; the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven; Grain 30 standing three mornings ahead, unbrought. The hand comes down on the river's next low note and the file lies open on the towel, complete, and worth nothing. Forward into Days 237–239 and the last market of Grain.
